components.explanation: Spatial makes this a three-dimensional surface program. Unshaded keeps fire independent of lights. The project uses Forward Plus with Direct Three D twelve. Forward Plus supports the ground Decal and scene S S I L; Compatibility would lose both. Without an explicit assignment, ALBEDO is white. COLOR carries vertex color, not a sampled texture.

This is the required color statement, unchanged. Remaining fire mixes red embers toward yellow heat and multiplies by intensity. Alpha is a separate decision: the shape and remaining fraction determine coverage. Fragment evaluates that shape across the surface. Moving its nonlinear shape calculation to four corner vertices would change the interpolated outline.

The CPU connection is four lines. After the hazard updates, this driver checks whether simulation is active, divides remaining duration by the cached initial duration, clamps the ratio, and writes the material parameter. It has no second damage timer. Every fire owns a material, while all of those materials share the same Shader resource.

A texture hint can change the numbers. These two samplers read exactly the same three pixels. The first declares source color and the other reads raw data. Both use nearest filtering and disable repetition, so texture filtering cannot explain the difference. The Boolean switches between the two paths without adding a correction factor.

Cargo needs three different kinds of texture. Albedo is color. Roughness is scalar data. The normal map is encoded direction data. Only albedo gets source color. All three repeat and use the same filtering. The normal sample goes through Godot's normal-map path, rather than being decoded as a color or assigned directly to NORMAL.

Here the surface stays lit. One scaled UV feeds all three textures, so a rust patch and its normal detail keep the same size. Roughness is clamped after scaling because the control reaches two. Normal strength goes to NORMAL MAP DEPTH. The shader writes no alpha and no metallic value, keeping the panel opaque and nonmetallic.

These values live on a material instance. The Shader holds declarations and defaults; a ShaderMaterial holds the current overrides and texture bindings. Two boxes can therefore use one program with different responses. Sharing the material itself would share the override too. The experiment changes the common program first, then changes only the first material's tint.

Godot's generated version reaches the same surface outputs with more general controls. It chooses a roughness channel, scales the sample, then assigns the normal texture and its depth. Its color sampler also declares source color, and its normal sampler does not. Saving the Shader alone does not save the converted material's texture bindings and current values.

excerpts.text:
ALBEDO = mix(ember_color.rgb, hot_color.rgb, fire_remaining) * intensity;
	ALPHA = clamp(shape * clamp(fire_remaining, 0.0, 1.0) * flicker, 0.0, 1.0);

func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
	if not is_instance_valid(hazard) or not is_instance_valid(hazard.game): return
	if not hazard.game.simulation_active(): return
	_material.set_shader_parameter("fire_remaining", clampf(hazard.lasting / initial_lasting, 0.0, 1.0))

shader = ExtResource("1_1coxp")
shader_parameter/albedo_tex = ExtResource("2_xq0y5")
shader_parameter/roughness_tex = ExtResource("4_hs00n")
shader_parameter/normal_tex = ExtResource("3_wus1a")
shader_parameter/uv_scale = 1.0
shader_parameter/tint_color = Color(1, 1, 1, 1)
shader_parameter/roughness_scale = 0.65
shader_parameter/normal_strength = 0.35

Now compare the three controlled values. At the center, full fire measures two ten, two ten, sixty seven. Half fire is one fifty eight, one twenty one, sixty seven. Zero returns the original background. Those are the values predicted before capture. Setting two produces a green channel of two fifty five: the Inspector range did not clamp the program's input.

Watch the bottle land, then the flame appear above its ground mark. The thrower keeps making new fires instead of restarting one shared color. During the pause, the lifetime value holds while the visual flicker can continue. Nine fires were recorded in this run. The explosive slug keeps a warning and burst; it does not acquire a flame mesh.

The top row returns sixty four, one twenty eight, and one ninety two. The lower row is visibly brighter: one thirty seven, one eighty eight, and two twenty five. The original prediction matches every center sample exactly. Missing the first decode leaves the raw values to be encoded again for display. This is why an albedo hint belongs on the sampler.

The normal comparison uses the same light and the same panel position. Raw Direct X reverses the green direction. Flipping its Y import setting makes it agree with the Open G L version within two display levels. The source map is very flat, so the visual difference is subtle. Raking light reveals it more clearly than the review light.

The scan makes the trade-offs visible. Small UV scale magnifies a small part of the sheet; eight repeats make the rust look much finer. Black tint hides most diffuse detail. Roughness two clips much of this map to fully rough. Normal strength two changes the raking light slightly, but cannot invent large dents that are absent from the texture.

First both panels respond when the shared shader's color statement changes. After restoring it, changing only A's tint alters the left panel; the right panel stays identical. This separates program sharing from value sharing. The actual base uses those two independent materials on crate stacks. Under its A C E S lighting, the weathered stack is darker.

This BoxMesh is rendered with that generated program and the three bound textures. It parses and draws, but it is kept out of the game. The hand-written cargo program has fewer controls because it solves a narrower job. The comparison also shows why a generated declaration is not a complete material: the textures and parameter overrides still have to be supplied.
